records.title: Support `Sentry.SourceGenerators` via Visual Studio 2019 version 16.11
records.notes: Build-time .NET SDK analyzer failure. Only sentry-dotnet example in the routing dataset, so holding it out leaves zero dotnet examples.

result.reason: The failure is in the Sentry .NET SDK's bundled Roslyn source generator during compilation. The analyzer cannot load Microsoft.CodeAnalysis 4.3.0 under Visual Studio 2019/UWP, and TreatWarningsAsErrors turns CS8032 into a build failure. This is SDK-specific rather than a Sentry SaaS application issue.
result.routing_history_summary: No prior transfers or ownership comments. Similar routing results were unrelated and provide no contrary evidence.
result.historical_evidence: No retrieved issue was a same-failure match. Historical search results were unrelated SaaS/UI or source-map issues and do not support a different destination.
result.next_action: Have the sentry-dotnet maintainers assess Roslyn/Visual Studio 2019 compatibility and source-generator packaging, including whether the analyzer should target an older Microsoft.CodeAnalysis version or be conditionally disabled.

records.title: Snuba seems to set timestamp_ms to a max value
records.notes: Self-hosted Snuba/ClickHouse timestamp error. Reporter-selected Product Area was Issues.

result.reason: The failure is in Sentry’s event-detail rendering path: malformed Snuba/ClickHouse timestamp data causes the UI request to return HTTP 500. No SDK-specific ownership is indicated, and the routing history contains no transfer or ownership dispute.
result.routing_history_summary: No prior transfers or comments. Similar routing examples are provisional STAY cases; confirmed self-hosted transfers involved deployment/storage/container concerns, unlike this product bug.
result.historical_evidence: No retrieved issue describes the same timestamp overflow failure. Issues 91617 and 102643 are background-only event-detail/500 problems with different symptoms and labels. Product Area: Issues best matches failure to display an event.
result.suspected_cause: Likely, the event-detail failure occurs in backend timestamp normalization: `timestamp_ms` is parsed into a Python datetime, and the ClickHouse max sentinel (`9999-12-31`) appears to overflow during conversion, producing the SnubaError. The current code search also shows frontend timestamp parsing, but its implementation could not be read within the tool budget.
result.next_action: Inspect and add regression coverage around `reformat_timestamp_ms_to_isoformat` in `src/sentry/api/utils.py`, plus the event timestamp schema in `src/sentry/snuba/events.py`, handling ClickHouse max-value sentinels before datetime conversion. The current default branch may differ from self-hosted 31.3.0.

records.title: sentry import global silently drops all but one ProjectKey per project
records.notes: Self-hosted user, but the root cause cited is in src/sentry (ProjectKey relocation import). A STAY prediction is defensible; a mismatch here is not necessarily an agent error.

result.reason: The defect is in the core global export/import relocation implementation (`ProjectKey.write_relocation_import`), not in an SDK or the self-hosted deployment wrapper. The report provides a precise reproduction and code-level failure: project-scoped get_or_create overwrites multiple keys and silently loses DSNs.
result.routing_history_summary: No transfers or ownership comments. Historical routing examples include relocation/import issues staying in getsentry/sentry; self-hosted transfer examples concern deployment-specific failures and are not comparable.
result.historical_evidence: No retrieved issue describes the same failure. Issue #83702 is related background on self-hosted-to-SaaS relocation, but does not establish this ProjectKey import behavior or ownership. Product Area: Org Relocation is selected because the failure occurs during global backup/relocation import.
result.suspected_cause: Likely `ProjectKey.write_relocation_import` uses project-only deduplication, causing multiple imported keys for one project to overwrite the same row rather than insert distinct keys. The reported public-key regeneration behavior should also be reviewed in the same method; the current default-branch code may differ from self-hosted 26.7.2.
result.next_action: Inspect and test `ProjectKey.write_relocation_import` at the cited model location, then add a round-trip test covering multiple keys per project and existing-key imports.

records.title: Taskworker KAFKA_TOPIC_OVERRIDES Ignored
records.notes: Helm-chart deployment, but the analysis points to taskworker code in src/sentry. Ambiguous ownership.

result.reason: The issue is specific to a self-hosted Helm deployment and its Kafka topic-prefix configuration. The reported failure occurs in the deployed self-hosted taskworker setup under strict Kafka ACLs, so getsentry/self-hosted is the best-supported destination.
result.routing_history_summary: No prior transfers or ownership comments. Historical routing includes confirmed transfers of taskworker/self-hosted operational failures to getsentry/self-hosted, including taskworker failures and missing event processing.
result.historical_evidence: Confirmed transfers: https://github.com/getsentry/self-hosted/issues/4241 (taskworker behavior), https://github.com/getsentry/self-hosted/issues/4276 (taskworker failure/no events), and https://github.com/getsentry/self-hosted/issues/4271 (taskworker resource issue). Similar-issue search found no same-failure match; results were only broad taskworker or self-hosted background.
result.next_action: Human maintainers should confirm whether the Helm chart or Sentry taskworker producer owns the fix, then route to the appropriate repository; if accepted in self-hosted, investigate propagation of real topic names through the taskbroker/Arroyo producer path.
